title: Speak to Potential, Not Limitations
html:
It amazes me that in a world overflowing with information and understanding there are people who casually label children asstupid,slow, ornot good enough.

Do they not realise those words don't just pass from their mouths through the air - they land. And they stick.

A single careless sentence can shape someone's sense of worth for decades.

A single encouraging phrase can do the same.

Think back. ... What words stuck with you?

Maybe someone said,"You'll never be able to do that," or"Be realistic," or"Things are tough out there."

Those sentences don't just describe a moment; they write rules you carry into adulthood.

Rules about what's possible.

Rules about who you think you are.

But here's the good news: You can rewrite those rules at any time.

And even better,you can help someone else rewrite theirs.

"You can do this."

"You've got the ability."

"You're capable of more than you think. "

Simple words. Massive impact. Especially if that person trusts you.

So, why choose destructive ones when encouragement takes the same amount of breath? Every interaction you have today is a chance to lift someone - including yourself.

This Week's Motivator

Pay attention to the words you use. Especially, the ones spoken casually, without thought. Make it a rule this week to speak to people in terms of what theycan do, not what they can't.

Prompt for the Week

Which words from your past are still shaping you, and which new words will you choose to replace them?
